claims.text: Which Country Reinvests the MOST in Fixed Assets?

claims.support: Indicator name: Gross fixed capital formation (% of GDP)

claims.text: A global look at gross fixed capital formation as a percentage of GDP, featuring Tanzania, Bhutan, China, the USA, and the UK.
The USA puts 21.3% of its economy into fixed assets, but one giant breaks this pattern.
Between the UK, the USA, and China, one reinvests a far larger share into fixed capital.
The UK puts 18.9% of its economy into fixed assets.
The USA puts 21.3%, putting income into infrastructure and equipment.
China charges ahead, putting 39.7% of its economy into fixed capital.
Yet Tanzania tops the world, putting 42.2% of its economy into fixed assets.
